craft_notes: Sthāyin: śṛṅgāra-vīra of sporting; vyabhicāri ullāsa at as-pleased conduct. Sanskrit-first: rundhe/vidadhe MIDDLE voices per UNC (kept middle — holding/melting unflattened); yathāruci (AS-PLEASED — kept; pleasure IS the conduct's rule). Rows: 9 (holding/melting/wiping triple — middle-voice acts), 1 (‘in my heart’ closes — sporting placed last, interior). Close: ‘sporting in my heart’. Rupture: semicolon (ground held, then taste ordained — dread held, wake tasted). Rejected: active-voice flatten — killed: middles kept; ‘play’ for sporting — killed: krīḍā kept sporting (house word). Read aloud: THIS-ground SHE-holds, DREAD-ful IN-split-ting WORLD-fear … HOLD-ing, MELT-ing, WIP-ing THE-foul-STRETCH-es, CON-duct AT-plea-SURE — SPORT-ing IN-my-HEART.

lines: This ground she holds, dreadful in splitting world fear;
this wake-fixed melted taste — ordained too. Holding, melting, wiping the foul stretches, conduct at pleasure — sporting in my heart.
l4.sanskrit_cite: imāṃ rundhe bhūmiṃ bhavabhayabhidātaṅkakaraṇīm | bhajati lasatāṃ sā mama hṛdi

reads_against.argmap: What ground holds, and what conduct sports? → Ground held dread-making; conduct as-pleased sporting in heart prayed.
c1_essence: Dread-ground held; as-pleased conduct sporting prayed.
